meaning: The number 245 appears in the Bible in connection with the return from the Babylonian exile, linked to practical counts of animals and people.
description: The number 245 is mentioned in two contexts in the historical books concerning the return from Babylon. In Ezra 2:66, it states that those who returned had 245 mules, as part of the census of their livestock and possessions. In Nehemiah 7:67, 245 singers and female singers are mentioned among those who returned. Both occurrences belong to the detailed lists of people and resources that accompanied the journey back to Judah after the exile. Although the number has no known deeper symbolic meaning, these records testify to the precise accounting that characterized the rebuilding of the Jewish community after the exile.

versions.meaning: The number 245 has no well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: 245 is not a number highlighted in the Bible or in classical Jewish numerology (gematria) with a widely recognized symbolic meaning. In gematria, the number may correspond to certain Hebrew words, but there is no broad tradition that assigns 245 a specific spiritual or symbolic role. It is not prominently linked to any known biblical event, law, or prophecy.
versions.reason: [major] The number 245 actually appears in the Bible, both in Ezra 2:66 (245 mules) and Nehemiah 7:67 (245 singers, male and female). Description claims that the number is not linked to any known biblical event, which is incorrect.; [major] The meaning field states that the number has no well-established symbolic significance but overlooks these concrete biblical occurrences. Although the number does not carry deep symbolic meaning, the meaning section should reflect that it actually appears in Scripture.; [minor] The gematria value of רָמָה (ramah, 'exalted/height') is 245, which could be mentioned in a footnote as an interesting linguistic observation.

footnotes.text: The lists in Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 are partially parallel but differ on some figures. Ezra 2:65 mentions 200 singers, male and female, while Nehemiah 7:67 gives 245. Such discrepancies may be due to different times of counting or copying errors in the transmission.
The Hebrew word רָמָה (ramah, 'height' or 'high place') has a gematria value of 245 (resh=200, mem=40, he=5). The word is used among other things as a place name in the Bible.
